title: $45,841 on paper from a bot that wins 27.7% of the time. The other end of the 51/51 thread
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Saw the 51/51 BTC thread this week asking whether a perfect win rate hides the risk. This card is the opposite problem, and I think it hides just as much.

Paper money, simulated, not advice.

The rule in one line: it watches groups of US stocks that usually move together, and when one lags while the others line up, it buys a daily call on the laggard and waits for it to catch up.

What the card says: 282 trades from 25 Aug to 30 Oct, 27.7% of them winners, +$45,841.23 realized, best streak 6 in a row.

What it doesn't say until you look at the curve: almost all of it arrived in a few weeks of September, and since then the line has drifted down a little every week. With fewer than 3 in 10 trades winning, a dozen or so trades carry the whole total, so 282 is a much smaller sample than it sounds.

The part I can't answer yet: is September a real edge on laggards catching up, or did a couple of sector rotations just happen to snap back inside the window? A low hit rate bot looks great right after a burst and bleeds premium the rest of the time. I'd rather someone here pokes a hole in it now than let the next two months do it.

How Quantradin helps with this: the card is out of Quantradin, which I built to test bots like this before anyone trusts them. The bot only ever sees bars that have already closed, and options buy at the ask and sell at the bid, so a burst like September has to survive the spread. Free to use, every dollar in it is paper.
